videos.desc: Mashed potatoes crispy fries 🍟                                          Crispy mashed potatoes  Ingredients 	•	Potatoes — 4 medium, 	•	Cornstarch — 2 tablespoons 	•	Salt — ½ tablespoon 	•	Black pepper — ½ tablespoon 	•	Paprika — ½ tablespoon 	•	Fresh coriander — 1 tablespoon, very finely chopped 	•	Oil — for deep frying Method of Preparation 	1.	Cut the potatoes into cubes and boil them in water for 7–8 minutes until just tender. 	2.	Drain the water and let the potatoes cool for 5 minutes. 	3.	Transfer the boiled potatoes into a bowl and mash them well. 	4.	Add cornstarch, salt, black pepper, paprika, and finely chopped coriander. 	5.	Mix everything well until a smooth mixture forms. 	6.	Transfer the mixture into a piping bag. 	7.	Rest the piping bag for 30 mins. 	8.	After resting, pipe the mixture and shape it with a knife. 	9.	Fry in medium heat oil until golden and crispy. #fries #chips #potato #fyp #foryoupage❤️❤️

Beef Paye 😍 ( winter recipe ) Ingredients: * 1.2 kg beef paya * 2 bay leaves * 2 cinnamon sticks * 2–3 green cardamoms * 4–5 cloves * 1 star anise * ½ tbsp whole black pepper * 1 tbsp cumin seeds * 1 tbsp turmeric powder * 1 tbsp red chili powder * 1½ tbsp salt * 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste * 1 tbsp oil * 1 diced onion * 5 cups water For the Tadka/Masala: * 5 tbsp oil * 1 finely chopped onion * 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste * 1 tbsp Kashmiri red chili powder * 1 tbsp cumin powder * 1 tbsp coriander powder * 1 tbsp homemade garam masala * ½ cup yogurt * 1 tbsp black pepper powder * 1 tbsp chili flakes Method: 1. Add beef paya, whole spices, powdered spices, salt, ginger-garlic paste, oil, onion and water to a pressure cooker. Cook for 30–35 minutes after the first whistle. 2. For the masala, heat oil and sauté onion. Add ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili, cumin, coriander and garam masala. Add yogurt and cook until the oil separates. 3. Add the cooked paya along with its yakhni to the masala. Add black pepper and chili flakes. 4. Simmer on low-medium heat for 5–10 minutes. 5. Serve hot with naan. #fyp #paye #beef #viral #cookingtales11

Chicken Kala Chana Pulao Ingredients: * 5 tbsp oil * 2 white onions, sliced * ½ chicken, cut into pieces * 2 tbsp tomato paste * 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste * 1 tbsp cumin powder * 1 tbsp garam masala * ½ cup yogurt * 1 tbsp black pepper powder * 1 tbsp salt * 1 cup boiled black chickpeas (kala chana) * 2 cups water * 1 cup soaked rice * Green chilies, chopped * Fresh coriander, chopped * Tomato slices Method: 1. Heat oil and fry the onions until golden brown. 2. Add chicken and fry until nicely browned. 3. Add tomato paste, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, garam masala, black pepper, salt, and yogurt. Mix well. 4. Cook over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until the water evaporates and the oil separates. 5. Add the boiled kala chana and mix well. 6. Add 2 cups water and boil for about 5 minutes. 7. Add the soaked rice, cover, and cook until the rice has absorbed the water and is tender. 8. Top with green chilies, fresh coriander, and tomato slices. 9. Cover and dum for 15 minutes. 10. Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot with raita. #viral #fyp #pulao #chicken #chickpeas

Dhaba-Style Mutton Palak …. My fvrt  Ingredients: * 500g boneless mutton * 5 tbsp oil * 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste * 1 tbsp chopped green chilies * 1 tbsp cumin seeds * 4–5 small white onions * 2 red tomatoes, sliced * ½ tbsp coriander powder * ½ tbsp cumin powder * ½ tbsp black pepper powder * 1 tbsp salt * 1½ cups water * Blanched & blended spinach * 2–3 whole red chilies Method: 1. Heat oil in a pressure cooker. Sauté ginger-garlic, green chilies and cumin. 2. Add mutton, onions, tomatoes, spices, salt and water. Mix well. 3. Pressure cook for 12–15 minutes after the first whistle. 4. Transfer to a pan and cook until the water evaporates and oil separates. 5. Add blanched & blended spinach and whole red chilies. Mix well. 6. Cover and cook on low flame for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally. 7. Serve hot with naan or paratha. #fyp #palak #mutton #viral #foryoupage❤️❤️

Masala Maggi (Late-night cravings) Ingredients: • 2 packets Maggi noodles • 4 tbsp oil • 1 chopped onion • ½ tbsp green chillies • 1 tbsp chopped garlic • 1 medium-sized chopped tomato • ½ chopped capsicum • 1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder • ¼ tbsp turmeric powder • A handful of fresh chopped coriander Method: 1. Heat oil, add onion, green chillies and garlic. Sauté well. 2. Add tomato, chilli powder and turmeric. Cook until soft. 3. Boil Maggi separately for 2 minutes and set aside. 4. Add capsicum to the masala gravy and sauté. 5. Add boiled Maggi and chopped coriander. Mix well. 6. Serve hot with your favourite sauce! #viral #fyp #maggi #noodles #quickrecipes

Chicken Changezi Ingredients; Chicken 1 tbsp paprika powder 1 tbsp coriander powder 1 tbsp cumin powder 4 tbsp yogurt 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste Juice of ½ lemon ½ tbsp black pepper powder 1 tbsp salt 5 tbsp oil 3 green cardamoms 1 black cardamom 1 bay leaf 2–3 cloves 1 cinnamon stick 2 medium white onions, chopped 1 tbs ginger garlic paste ¼ tbsp turmeric powder A pinch of kasuri methi 3 tomatoes, blended into a paste ½ glass water ¼ cup fresh cream 2–3 green chillies Fresh coriander, chopped Method: Marinate chicken with all spices, yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt for 2 hours. Heat oil, add whole spices and sauté. Add onions and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, kasuri methi, turmeric and tomato paste. Cook until oil separates. Fry marinated chicken separately until lightly golden. Add chicken to the gravy with ½ glass of water. Cover and cook for 10 minutes. Add green chillies and cream. Mix well. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with naan or paratha. #fyp #viral #chickenchangezi #cookingtales11 #cooking

Badami Mutton Qorma Ingredients: * 5 tbsp oil * 2 sliced white onions * 800g boneless mutton * 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste * 1 bay leaf * 3–4 cloves * 3 green cardamoms * 1 star anise * 1 cinnamon stick * ¼ tbsp whole black pepper * ½ tbsp cumin seeds * 1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder * 1 tbsp coriander powder * 1 tbsp salt (adjust to taste) * 2½ cups warm water * 1 tbsp cumin powder * 4 tbsp Greek yogurt * ½ tbsp black pepper powder * ¼ cup water * 2 tbsp almond powder Method: 1. Fry onions until golden, remove and set aside. 2. In the same oil, sauté whole spices and ginger garlic paste. Add mutton and fry. 3. Add chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Mix well. Add warm water and cumin powder. Cover and cook for 1 hour and 15 minutes, until the mutton is tender. 4. Add Greek yogurt, crushed fried onions and black pepper. Cook until the gravy thickens and oil separates. 5. Mix almond powder with ¼ cup water, add to the gravy and cook covered for few minutes. Serve hot with homemade naan. #fyp #viral #qorma #mutton #foryoupage❤️❤️

Crispy Wavy Chips! 🌶️✨Don’t forget to make these for snack time😍 Ingredients: 3 potatoes ¼ tbsp garlic powder ¼ tbsp salt ¼ tbsp dried parsley ¼ tbsp milk powder ¼ tbsp chilli flakes ¼ tbsp paprika powder Method of Preparation: Cut the potatoes into wavy chips using a wavy cutter. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes.Drain and pat completely dry, ensuring no moisture remains. Fry in medium-hot oil until slightly golden.Mix all the seasoning ingredients and sprinkle over the chips. Toss well and enjoy your crispy, flavourful wavy chips! #fyp #chips #wavy #snacks #viral

Have you ever tried this delicious Aloo Palak Keema? 😍 Ingredients: 2 potatoes, cut into cubes 500 g beef mince (keema) 600 g spinach (palak) 1 onion, chopped 3 tomatoes, chopped 5 tbsp oil 1 tbsp cumin seeds 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste 1 tbsp green chilli paste 1 tbsp salt 1 tbsp red chilli powder Method of Preparation: Heat oil and fry the cubed potatoes until slightly golden. Remove and set aside. In the same oil, add cumin seeds, ginger-garlic paste and green chilli paste. Sauté, then add the chopped onion and fry until slightly golden. Add tomatoes, salt and beef mince. Mix, cover and cook on low heat for 5–8 minutes. Remove the lid and mix well. Add red chilli powder and stir. Add spinach, mix well, cover and cook until the spinach becomes tender. Add the fried potatoes and cook until everything is completely cooked. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with naan. #fyp #alo #viral #palak #spinach

Who would love to have this Chana Masala (Chole) 🥘 for breakfast every day 😍 Ingredients: 2 cups chickpeas, soaked overnight 2 bay leaves 3 green cardamoms 4–5 cloves 5 tbsp oil 2 red tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp coriander powder 1 tbsp cumin powder 1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder ½ cup yogurt ½ cup fried onions ¼ cup cashews ¼ cup fresh coriander 5–6 garlic cloves 1-inch ginger piece ½ cup water 1 tbsp black pepper powder 1 tbsp salt Method of Preparation: Add soaked chickpeas, water, bay leaves, cardamoms and cloves to a pressure cooker. Cook for 15–20 minutes after the first whistle, until tender. Heat oil in a pan, add chopped tomatoes, coriander powder, cumin powder and Kashmiri red chilli powder. Cook well. Blend yogurt, fried onions, cashews, fresh coriander, garlic and ginger into a smooth paste. Add the paste to the tomato mixture and cook well. Add 1 cup boiled chickpeas, ½ cup water, black pepper and salt. Mix and simmer until the curry thickens. For the tadka, heat oil and add cumin seeds and whole green chillies. Pour over the chana. Serve hot with paratha, naan or rice. #fyp #chickpeas #chole #chana #viral

Lahm Mandi  Ingredients: 1 kg mutton 5 tbsp oil 2 white onions, chopped 1 tbsp cumin seeds ½ tbsp whole black pepper 2 cinnamon sticks 2 bay leaves 5–6 cloves 1 black cardamom 2–3 green cardamoms 1 tbsp coriander powder 1 tbsp cumin powder 2 dried lemons 1 tbsp black pepper powder 1 tbsp salt 2 cups warm water, plus ½ cup extra 1 tbsp biryani masala 1 glass rice, soaked for 3 hours Food colouring, as needed Method of Preparation: Heat oil in a pressure cooker and fry the onions until slightly golden. Add the mutton and fry well.Add the whole spices and cook for 2–3 minutes. Add 2 cups warm water,and add all the spices mentioned above . Bring to a boil, close the lid and pressure-cook for 15–20 minutes after the first whistle. Allow the pressure to release naturally. Remove the mutton and some excess oil from the yakhni. Mix 1 tbsp biryani masala with the reserved yakhni oil and brush it over the meat. Grill for 2–3 minutes. Add ½ cup extra water to the remaining yakhni, if needed. Add the soaked rice and bring to a boil. Close the cooker and cook for 2–3 minutes after the first whistle. Release the pressure, add food colouring and leave the rice on dum for another 10 minutes. Transfer the rice to a serving plate, arrange the grilled mutton on top and enjoy! #viral #lahmmandi #fyp #mutton #trending

You can make Nutella at home🍫 @Giovanni Siracusa  INGREDIENTS: 450 g raw blanched hazelnuts 165g powdered sugar 38g unsweetened cocoa powder 60g neutral-flavored oil 8 g vanilla extract Pinch of salt INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Spread the hazelnuts on a baking sheet and roast for 10-12 minutes, until lightly golden and fragrant. 2. Transfer the warm hazelnuts to a high-powered blender. Blend for 3-8 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed, until smooth and creamy like nut butter. 3. Add the powdered sugar, cocoa powder, oil, vanilla extract, and salt. 4. Blend again until completely smooth and glossy, scraping down the sides as needed. 5. Transfer to a clean, airtight glass jar and enjoy! NOTE: The Nutella will naturally thicken as it cools. Store in the refrigerator to keep it fresh. #food #chocolate #nutella #fyp

Tarte au chocolat is easier than you think Recipe: (for the chocolate crust) - 2 boxes of @Simple Mills Chocolate Brownie Sweet Thins - 3-4 tbsp of melted coconut or butter (for the chocolate filing) - 400g / 14 oz of baking chocolate - 1 can (400ml / 13.5 oz) full fat coconut milk - 2 tsp of vanilla extract - In a food processor (or blender) blend the Sweet Thins until fine, then blend in the melted butter or oil - Press your crust into a 9-inch tart pan using your hand or a spatula - Let solidify in the fridge for about 1 hour - Melt your baking chocolate and whisk in the coconut milk and vanilla extract - Pour into the tart pan (make sure it doesn’t surpass the crust) - Refrigerate for about 1 hour or until firm #simplemillspartner #food #chocolate #dessert #fyp

Cheese crackers made of 4 ingredients (cheez-its) Recipe: - 200g (about 2 cups / 7 oz) of shredded parmigiano reggiano cheese (I’m 99% certain that cheddar will also work) - 1 cup flour - 4 tbsp cold butter - 3 tbsp cold water - Salt (optional) - Garlic powder (optional) - Onion powder (optional) - In a food processor, blend the shredded cheese, flour, salt, spices and butter - Then blend in the water… (if your food processor isn’t good then mix it by hand) - Form into a ball, cover it, and refrigerate for one hour… (this step isn’t necessary but it will be easier to roll out afterwards) - Preheat oven to 350F - Roll out the dough flat, then cut into squares and with a toothpick or chopstick poke holes in the middle - Top with a light coating of salt - Bake at 350F for 12 minutes #food #healthy #snack #cheese #fyp

save my favorite childhood meal: pork rib, potato, green bean stew or 排骨炖豆角 🩷  ep 1: homesick - let me know in the comments your childhood meals and I’ll try to recreate :))  Ingredients: • 2 lb pork ribs, cut into pieces • 1 lb green beans, trimmed • 2 medium potatoes, cut into chunks • 15–20g rock sugar • 3 tbsp light soy sauce • 1 tbsp dark soy sauce • 2 tbsp Shaoxing cooking wine • 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional) • 5–6 slices ginger • 4 cloves garlic • 2 scallions • 2 star anise • 2 bay leaves • 1 small cinnamon stick • 1½ tbsp neutral oil • 700–900ml hot water • ½–1 tsp salt, to taste Instructions: 1. Blanch the ribs: Add pork ribs to a pot of cold water with a few ginger slices and a splash of Shaoxing wine. Bring to a boil, cook for 3–5 minutes, then drain and rinse. 2. Caramelize the sugar: Heat oil in a pot over medium-low heat. Add rock sugar and stir until melted and amber-colored. Add ribs and toss to coat. 3. Build the flavor: Add ginger, garlic, scallions, star anise, bay leaves, and cinnamon. Stir-fry for about 1 minute until fragrant. 4. Season & simmer: Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and oyster sauce (if using). Pour in enough hot water to mostly cover the ribs. Cover and simmer on low for 35–45 minutes. 5. Add the veggies: Add green beans and simmer for 10 minutes, then add potatoes and cook for another 10–15 minutes, until everything is tender. 6. Reduce the sauce: Remove the lid, increase to medium-high heat, and let the sauce reduce for 10–15 minutes until rich and glossy. Season with salt to taste. #childhoodmeal #chinesediet #chineserecipe #homecooking #momscooking

videos.desc: This is 1,105 lbs on my back... and my goal was to hold it in a support for 1 minute.  Did I make it? You'll have to watch and see... I currently weigh 174 lbs, so this was about 6.3 times my bodyweight. Now, in general, heavy supports like this are incredible for developing connective tissue strength. The time spent under heavy load creates and incredibly strong stimulus for the body to build that connective tissue. I find they're also incredible for developing thickness and strength in the entire back.  They're one of "secret weapon" exercises for the back development I've got (loaded carries are one of the other ones). Naturally, you don't start with weights like this, or work up to them quickly. I've been doing supports like this since about the 4th year I was training, which at this point was 32 years ago. I'm 52 years old right now and because I've been regularly been doing holds like this for decades, I have no worries about injuries from doing this. But that's ME. I did these yesterday (as of writing this) and I have very little muscle soreness and no strains. My back feels great and my spine feels awesome. If you wanted to start doing supports like this, I would recommend starting with your current 1 RM squat weight.  Hold that for a minute and see how it feels. You'd be starting with a weight your body knows it can handle. I also have a program that uses connective training called "Return to Prime" (it's specifically targeted for training to maintain and build muscle after 40). --------------- Got a lagging muscle group or exercise? Try this free 3 week program.... Link in bio #heavysupports #lockoutholds #squatsupports #connectivetissuetraining #nicknilsson

If I could only do one tricep exercise, this would be it...Bodyweight Tricep Extensions. This is my absolute favorite exercise for building monster triceps. It puts a fantastic stretch particularly on the long head of the triceps (the biggest of the three heads) while also putting a "normal" stretch on the medial and lateral heads. This lengthened-position tension I find gives a very strong growth stimulus. As a case study, I present myself :) This is an exercise I started doing regularly in my first few years of training. For this setup, I've got a bar loaded with 45's braced up against the front of the power rack.  I find the height to be perfect for this exercise for me and because the bar spins freely, it allows me to maintain a good wrist position. You can set a bar up on the rack rails (or use a Smith machine bar) to set the height to wherever you feel comfortable. That works great, too. To build mass, keep to a 5-7 rep range on the sets (2-3 sets is good, pushing to near failure). The higher the bar and the closer your feet are to it, the less resistance you'll get on the exercise. I've used this exercise setup when training complete beginners, with the bar set to about midsection level and feet set very close to the bar. You can make it so the resistance is almost nothing. To make it harder, you lower the bar and/or move your feet further back. This puts more bodyweight loading onto the triceps. When you get strong enough, you can then start elevating your feet (I've got my feet up on a bench here). Then you can start doing single arm bodyweight extensions. Personally, I progressed to the point where I could do near-VERTICAL bodyweight tricep extensions... my body was literally almost in a handstand position, doing the exercise with basically my entire bodyweight. This took me years to build up to and is INCREDIBLY difficult to do. --------------- Want big, giant meatloaf triceps? Try this free 3 week specialization program.... Link in bio #tricepextensions #calisthenics #tricepexercise #bigarms #nicknilsson

I couldn't resist... this is a combination of the Floating Bar Pull-Up with my Barbell Clamp Pull-Up.  Going to call it a Viltrumite Pull-Up (if you look up Viltrumite, you'll see why!). Yes, this is my idea of fun... yes it looks just CRAZY... and no I don't expect (or recommend!) anybody try this one unless you've got a VERY strong grip! Sometimes I just like to try insane stuff to see what's physically possible for me (training for 35+ years will do that to you!). This one was TOUGH. I did 3 sets of 2 reps and my grip was torched...the second rep came close to opening up my grip in each set. I've got 95 lbs on the bar for the clamping part and 65 lbs on the bar for the foot part. I THINK that's about as far as I can take this one... but you never know... --- Want a bigger, stronger back?  Try THIS program for 3 weeks... Link in bio #pullups #weightedpullups #traininsane #calisthenics #nicknilsson

Bench pressing on a linear row machine? So...you know I like coming up with stuff that uses equipment in... "different" ways... :) Last week, I posted about the linear T-Bar "antler grip" rowing machine from @MikoloFitness  It's a cool piece of equipment and naturally, I had to come up with a few other things I could do with it, including what is actually a really good single-arm press setup. I REALLY like using it for rear delt work as well... just a small shift in body position (moving your chest down lower so the pad is just under your chin) really lines up the rear delts perfectly. And, of course... there are a few other good rowing variations you can use it for that really hit nice. If you'd like to get one of these, use code NICK5 for 5% off. I've got a direct link in my bio so you can check it out. #linearrow #mikoloblackfive #BlackFriday #BFCM #nicknilsson

See-Saw Pushdowns... and yes you CAN "just do cable pushdowns"... I'm not saying you can't or that this is necessarily better! This is a unique setup that can come in handy if you don't have access to a high pulley or are just looking for a way to mix things up in your tricep training. It's a simple see-saw setup with the bar set over the bench, one end loaded and the other not loaded. You kneel down and set your hands on the fat, rolling end of the bar and do leverage pushdowns. That's literally it! On the next set, face the other way to keep things even (the bar does sit an angle for most of the exercise). It's quick and easy to set up and actually works really well. --------------- Want bigger triceps? Try this free 3 week specialization program... Link in bio #pushdowns #triceps #triceppushdowns #tricepexercise #nicknilsson

One Arm Barbell Body Drag Curl for biceps... this is a variation of the Vince Gironda exercise, the body drag curl. This version is done using a regular Olympic bar, just holding it with one hand. I like this for changing the exercise up a bit.  It gives you more grip and forearm work and allows you to rotate the bar to get a bit more supination during the exercise. For me personally, I also found this easier on my shoulder tweak, bringing the elbows up and behind the body.  It takes loading off the anterior delt (and associated structures) that way, which is what I need right now. --------------- Got a lagging muscle group or exercise? Try this free 3 week specialization program... Link in bio #bodydragcurl #bicepcurl #dragcurl #gironda #nicknilsson

I call these Chest Pulldowns... this is shoulder-friendly pec maintenance training, not necessarily for hypertrophy or strength. While in the process of dealing with a shoulder injury, I want to keep up a base level of training on the chest without causing any further injury, which means avoiding traditional pressing with any substantial weight. It's kind of a mash-up of a cable cross-over and a band pulldown, using the bands around the elbows to PUSH downwards and in while leaning and hunching forwards to put the pecs in the better position to contract (versus the lats, which are also somewhat active in this movement). The hands do grip on the bands but only to maintain arm position...the action should primarily be a push down and in with the elbows. The setup put my shoulders in a good position to activate the pecs with decent resistance but without putting extra torque into the shoulder joint by pressing. This results in horizontal adduction (bringing the arms inwards towards the mid-line of the body) without pressing and without elbow extension. Having the resistance being closer to the shoulder joint also helped, I think.  It allowed me to work the chest relatively hard with basically zero (at least for my particular issue) pain in the shoulder joint. For setup, it's simply two medium-thickness bands attached around the top corners of the rack.  I found this gave me a good angle of pull and enough resistance to get really good tension in the chest from it. As I mentioned, it's a not a serious chest-builder but I can feel it'll definitely help me maintain chest mass and strength while I rehab my shoulder. --------------- Got a lagging muscle group or exercise? Try this free 3 week specialization program... Link in bio #chestexercise #cablecrossover #shoulderinjury #chestworkout #nicknilsson

Single Kettlebell Farmers Cycling... ok, that's not really a thing, but now it is. Very simple concept... I'm holding a 90 lb kettlebell in one hand while I do HIIT on the stationary bike. This is VERY challenging to the core and really got my quads pumped up like crazy. Definitely start with lighter weight, but I found holding just the one kettlebell (or a dumbbell is fine) is the best way to go because it keeps one hand free for getting on and off and adjusting resistance. The key is to know that the bike you're using has enough weight capacity to accommodate your bodyweight and the weight - mine is rated to 350 lbs so well within. And honestly, the 90 lbs was plenty for weight.  I don't a see a need to go higher than that. It was just brutal on the core. Then I was just doing 20-30 seconds at pretty close to the highest resistance level of the bike then switching hands and going again for 20-30 seconds. I like this method a lot. Got great cardio, core and quad training out of it. --------------- Got a lagging muscle group or exercise? Try this free 3 week specialization program... Link in bio #cardio #hiit #loadedcarry #farmerscarry #nicknilsson

Been testing out this linear T-Bar "antler grip" rowing machine from @MikoloFitness for the past few weeks. Overall, I really like it. It has a good weight capacity (220 lbs) for a home gym piece and a nice, smooth action (makes a little noise but nothing crazy). If you're super strong on rows, you can easily switch over to single arm rows and it'll stay on track just fine. The antler grip gives you a ton of options for targeting different areas of your back (depending on which handles you grip and how you grip them). This is definitely one of the standout features of this rowing machine. If you have trouble feeling your back working or if you have a tendency to swing or heave when doing rows (or if your lower back isn't in the best shape), the chest support will keep you in place. If you'd like to get one of these (the price is actually very reasonable, I think), use code NICK5 for 5% off. I've got a direct link in my bio so you can check it out. #tbarrow #mikoloblackfive #BlackFriday #BFCM #nicknilsson

I'm still dealing with a tweaked right shoulder that hurts when I do any pressing movements... this is one of the methods I'm using to work around it and with it to get it back in business. This is an Offset Load Dumbbell Bench Press - I've got a 75 lb dumbbell in my left hand and literally a FIVE pound dumbbell in my right hand. The heavier side gives a stronger training stimulus, obviously, but the five pound dumbbell is so light that I can do a full range of motion with the injured side. There IS carryover (specifically via the nervous system) between the two sides of your body. You can actually still the SEE the activation in my right pec, even with an extremely light weight. This type of training serves two purposes... maintain strength in BOTH sides of the body and keep the injured side moving so that I can circulation through the area. Circulation is absolutely key to recovery.   In my experience (based on a doctors advice that I got 30 years ago when I had a bad ankle injury), I've found I get better recovery results by keeping the area moving through a good range of motion and under at least a light load. The key for me is to let pain be the guide... if it's a sharp pain, I don't do it.  If it's more of a dull ache, I'll do it with very little resistance and focus on just moving the joint (like I'm doing here). That being said, that's ME and my own way of moving forward with recovery.  --------------- Want to build a bigger, stronger chest? Try this free 3 week specialization program... Link in bio #benchpress #dumbbellpress #shoulderrehab #shoulderinjury #nicknilsson

Two Vertical Bar Pull-Ups done for reps... I've showed versions of this before (a weighted version with this exact setup). I've got two regular Olympic bars set up vertically in a stack of bumper plates.  This holds them up very effectively... not without a bit of shifting, but mostly stable. This time I just did it for max reps (got 13). This setup has two major benefits... 1. The rotating bar ends allow your shoulders to move naturally as you do the exercise. I start in an almost pronated position at the bottom, the rotate to a more neutral almost supinated position at the top. 2. The smooth, thick surface challenges your grip strength a LOT.  In order to not slide down the bar, you have to really grip hard. When doing these, I like to pull up as high as I can and really focus on engaging the lats towards the top. This is one of my favorite setup for pull-ups... it's not ideal in a busy gym, but in a home gym with the available equipment, it's awesome. --------------- Want to build a bigger, stronger back? Try this free 3 week specialization program... Link in bio #pullups #calisthenics #gripstrength #backexercise #nicknilsson

Kneeling Leaning Curls... in 36+ years of training, I've never used this simple body position technique before and DANG does it hit nice. I'm down in a single leg kneeling position, curling on the same side as the forward knee (left knee forward, left arm curl). I'm using just a 25 lb dumbbell here...no need to go heavy here. The biceps love focused tension on isolation exercises like this. The key is that at the bottom of the curl, I'm leaning AWAY from that side (you can see it more after a few reps when I change to a head-on view). This leaning back and away puts a GREAT stretch on the biceps at the bottom...comparable to an incline curl. Then you curl up, like a normal curl, which also gives you excellent tension all the way to the top. Keep your palm facing forward the entire time - no rotation of the forearm.  This will keep the tension on the biceps better. I only showed the left arm here because my right shoulder is still a bit tweaked and that stretch at the bottom didn't sit well with it. But you can potentially go right into curling with the other arm, since it's not getting worked, or you can take a short rest to catch your breath or let your nervous system get a bit of recovery. --------------- Want to build big arms? Try this free 3 week specialization program... Link in bio #curls #dumbbellcurls #biceps #bicepcurls #nicknilsson

Leg Hook Single Leg Sissy Squats...can't wait to see the comments on this one! I know... it just gets weirder and weirder around here :)   This one is like creating a sissy squat machine (probably in your home gym... I do have self-awareness ;). Essentially, you're using a bar set on the rack (or a Smith machine bar) with your leg hooked over the bar to create a rotating pivot for doing a single leg sissy squat. As strange as it looks, it's actually an excellent way to do controlled sissy squats one leg at a time. You get the great stretch on the quads with a lot less stress on the knees (in my experience at least) because the knee hook controls the movement AND allows you control the amount of bodyweight loading you're using for the exercise. This one won't be a banger for everybody but for the right person, it will be. The setup is very simple... literally just set the rails of the rack (or the Smith machine bar) to about mid-thigh height when standing. Bring your leg over then hook your knee on the bar. Hold the bar with both hands then bend your working knee, coming down into the bottom of the sissy squat. Make sure you get that good stretch at the bottom then use quad activation to extend the knee and come back. You can go straight into the other leg when doing these since the other leg isn't getting worked. If you try it, let me know how you like it! --------------- Want to build bigger, stronger legs? Try this free 3 week specialization program... Link in bio #sissysquat #quads #quadexercise #legtraining #nicknilsson

What's going on guys? I usually don't really post quotes on my TikTok and things like that, but I do it a lot on my Instagram just to give people a perspective on what goes through my mind on a day-to-day basis, especially at night before I lay my head down to rest. I always have you guys in my mind whenever I'm thinking about things like that. What words can I say to encourage you, inspire you, motivate you to go out there and become a better man or woman that you always wanted to be? And let you guys know what I go through on a day-to-day basis and what I think about on a day-to-day basis that help influence my decisions as a man who is on the journey of becoming the best version of himself in all aspects, in all areas of life, right? And you are more than capable of achieving and accomplishing anything you want to do. And some of the biggest things that you should want to do is to become the best person you can be for other people as well, right? Everything shouldn't be a selfish thing, but you should want to be selfless. You want to get back to people, whether that's financially, physically, emotionally, spiritually, things of that nature. There is a lot more to life than just the gym. But like I always say, the gym is the biggest centerpiece of self-improvement and you can meet your lover, your best friend, a community of people. 🍌 Low-Calorie & High-Protein Bananenbrot 🤍 perfekt als Meal Prep, gesundes Frühstück oder süßer Snack für zwischendurch 🥹🤍 🤍 ca. 370 kcal I ca. 39 g Protein Zutaten: * 50 g Banane * 25 g Mehl / Dinkelmehl * 25 g Cinnalicious Proteinpulver (meins ist von More) * 3 g Backpulver * 1 Ei (Größe M) * 100 g Skyr * 1 Scoop Chunky Flavour (ich benutze „Banana Chocolate Split“ von Rocka, alternativ Erythrit) * 50 ml Wasser * 1 Prise Salz Zubereitung: 1. Zuerst alle trockenen Zutaten (Mehl, Proteinpulver, Backpulver, Chunky Flavour und Salz) in einer Schüssel miteinander vermischen. 2. Die Banane mit einer Gabel zerdrücken und zusammen mit dem Ei, Skyr und Wasser zu den trockenen Zutaten geben. 3. Alles gut miteinander verrühren, bis ein gleichmäßiger Teig entsteht. 4. Den Teig in eine kleine, ofenfeste Form geben. 5. Bei 180 °C Ober-/Unterhitze ca. 20–23 Minuten backen. 6. Anschließend abkühlen lassen und genießen! 🤎 Mein Tipp: Ich backe es immer nur 20 Minuten und stelle es anschließend für ein paar Stunden in den Kühlschrank. Dadurch bekommt es die perfekte, richtig saftige Konsistenz!! 🥹🤌🏼 Große Empfehlung! Auch perfekt als Meal Prep geeignet! Einfach am Abend vorher vorbereiten, über Nacht im Kühlschrank aufbewahren und am nächsten Morgen direkt genießen. Schmeckt gekühlt meiner Meinung nach sogar noch besser! Aktuell mein Favorit! Unbedingt abspeichern & ausprobieren! 🫶🏼 #highprotein #lowcalorie #mealprep #bananenbrot #proteinrezepte

If you have 10 minutes & just a few ingredients then you have dinner on the table! 🍽️ Roasted Red Pepper & Ravioli Soup  Details below:  1 lb ground beef  32oz carton tomato & roasted red pepper soup  1 bag frozen cheese ravioli  1-2 cups spinach  Parmesan cheese  1/2 tsp of each salt, pepper, garlic powder & Italian seasoning  - brown ground beef in a large pan on medium heat - Use a paper towel to dab excess grease if needed  - Add soup and bring to a simmer, add frozen ravioli, reduce to medium-low heat, cover  - Cook for an additional 5-7 minutes, once ravioli is done add spinach and Parmesan  - I served mine with sourdough garlic cheese bread 🤤 #creatorsearchinsights #easymealanddinnerideas #10minutemeal #onepandinner #easydinnerideas

Chicken & Vegetable Soup 🍅🍲 A cozy, hearty chicken and vegetable soup with roasted tomatoes that add SO much flavor! The kind of dinner that tastes like you spent all day making it, without actually having to! INGREDIENTS * Roma tomatoes, halved or quartered depending on size * Olive oil * Salt & pepper, to taste * 1 yellow onion, diced * 2 large carrots, chopped * 2 celery stalks, chopped * Baby potatoes, sliced into rounds * 1–1½ lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts * 1 tsp salt * 1 tsp garlic powder * ½ tsp black pepper * 1 (32 oz) carton chicken bone broth * 1–2 cups green beans, halved INSTRUCTIONS 1. Preheat oven to 425°F. Halve or quarter the Roma tomatoes and spread onto a sheet pan. Drizzle generously with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 30–35 minutes until softened and beautifully roasted. 2. Meanwhile, chop the onion, carrots, and celery, and slice the baby potatoes into rounds. 3. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped vegetables and potatoes and sauté for about 5 minutes. 4. Season chicken breasts with 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, and ½ tsp pepper. Add to the pot and sear for approximately 3 minutes per side. 5. Pour in the entire 32 oz carton of bone broth. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for approximately 45 minutes, or until the chicken reaches 165°F and the potatoes are fork-tender. 6. Remove the chicken and shred. Add the halved green beans to the pot, cover, and continue simmering on low for about 15 minutes, until tender. 7. Return the shredded chicken to the pot along with the roasted tomatoes. Stir everything together, allow to heat through, and season to taste with additional salt and pepper as needed. Serve warm and enjoy! 🤍 SAVE this one for your next cozy dinner night, and follow @cooking.with.brig for more easy, family-friendly meals! #creatorsearchinsights #easydinnerideas #easydinner #cozysoup #chickensoup

STEAK YUM YUM BOWLS 🥩🍚🥑 Full recipe 👇🏼 and don’t forget to follow along so you don’t miss what we are making next!  INGREDIENTS For the bowls: * Cooked jasmine rice * Shredded carrots * Shredded purple cabbage (optional, but I love the extra crunch!) * Cucumber, cut into bite-size pieces * Avocado, sliced or diced * Primal Kitchen Yum Yum Sauce For the steak: * 1–1½ lbs ribeye or top sirloin steak, cut into bite-size pieces * Salt * Black pepper * Garlic powder * 1 tbsp chili crunch oil (more or less depending on your spice preference) INSTRUCTIONS 1. Season the steak: Cut steak into bite-size pieces and add to a bowl. Drizzle with chili crunch oil and season generously with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Toss until every piece is thoroughly coated. 2. Air fry: Preheat air fryer to 390°F. Arrange steak in a single layer and air fry for approximately 9 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through, or until cooked to your liking. Cooking time will vary depending on the size of your steak pieces and your air fryer. 3. Prep the bowls: While the steak cooks, prepare your jasmine rice and chop your veggies. 4. Assemble: Start with a bed of fluffy jasmine rice. Add shredded carrots, purple cabbage (if using), cucumber, steak, and avocado. 5. Finish: Drizzle generously with Primal Kitchen Yum Yum Sauce and serve! #creatorsearchinsights #easydinnerideas #easydinner #steakbowl #healthybowls

TRADER JOE’S DINNERS THAT PRACTICALLY MAKE THEMSELVES — PART 6! 🍝 This Meatball & Ravioli Bake might be one of the easiest yet! And the secret ingredient? Trader Joe’s Tomato & Roasted Red Pepper Soup instead of traditional pasta sauce! INGREDIENTS * 2 packages Trader Joe’s Cheese Ravioli (refrigerated, uncooked) * 1 package Trader Joe’s Frozen Turkey Meatballs (thawed) * 3 cups Trader Joe’s Tomato & Roasted Red Pepper Soup * ½ tsp black pepper * 1 tsp garlic powder * 1 tsp Italian seasoning * ½ tsp dried oregano * ¼–½ tsp red pepper flakes (adjust to taste) * 2 handfuls fresh spinach * 1–1½ cups shredded mozzarella cheese INSTRUCTIONS 1. Preheat oven to 400°F. 2. Add uncooked ravioli, thawed turkey meatballs, and tomato & roasted red pepper soup to a 9×13 baking dish. 3. Add seasonings and stir until everything is evenly coated. 4. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30–35 minutes, or until the ravioli is tender and meatballs are heated through. 5. Remove from oven, add spinach, and stir into the sauce. 6. Generously top with mozzarella and return to the oven, uncovered, for about 5 minutes. 7. Broil for the last 1–2 minutes until golden and bubbly, watching closely! Save this one for the next night you need dinner to practically make itself! 🤍 Follow @cooking.with.brig for more insanely easy Trader Joe’s dinners! #TraderJoesRecipes #EasyDinnerIdeas #RavioliBake   #creatorsearchinsights #traderjoesturkeymeatballs

CALABRIAN CHICKEN & RICE BAKE 🫑🧅🧀 Another Trader Joe’s dinner that practically makes itself! 👏🏼 Everything goes into ONE baking dish, the oven does almost all the work, and you end up with tender shredded chicken, flavorful rice, peppers, onions, and a bubbly layer of melted mozzarella. Minimal effort, minimal cleanup, and SO much flavor! INGREDIENTS: * 1⅓ cups Calabrian chili sauce (add more if you like it extra saucy!) * 1½ cups uncooked jasmine rice * 2½ cups chicken broth * 1 large bell pepper, thinly sliced (I used ½ red + ½ green) * 1 yellow onion, thinly sliced * 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts * 1 tsp salt * 1 tsp garlic powder * ½ tsp black pepper * ½ tsp dried oregano * ½ tsp smoked paprika * Shredded mozzarella cheese, for topping INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Lightly grease a 9×13 baking dish. 2. Add Calabrian sauce, rice, and chicken broth. Stir to combine. 3. Add sliced peppers and onion. 4. Season chicken with salt, garlic powder, pepper, oregano, and smoked paprika. Nestle into the rice mixture. 5. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40–45 minutes. 6. Stir the rice and check for doneness. If needed, cover and bake another 10 minutes, until rice is tender, liquid absorbed, and chicken reaches 165°F. 7. Remove chicken, shred, and stir back into the rice. 8. Top generously with mozzarella. Bake uncovered about 5 minutes until melted and bubbly. Broil the last 1–2 minutes if desired! NOTES: 🌶️ Add extra sauce if you like it saucier. 🍚 Rice still firm? Don't worry! Ovens vary. Simply cover tightly with foil and return to the oven for another 5–10 minutes until tender. 🍗 If chicken reaches 165°F before the rice is done, remove it while the rice finishes. Save this one for an easy dinner night! 🤍 #TraderJoesRecipes #EasyDinnerIdeas #OnePanDinner  #creatorsearchinsights #traderjoesmeal

Finally getting around to trying the viral Caramelized onion pasta!!  INGREDIENTS * 2 large sweet onions, thinly sliced * 2 whole heads of garlic * Olive oil, for drizzling * 2 tsp paprika, divided * 1 tsp salt, divided * 1 tsp black pepper, divided  * 2 tbsp fresh thyme leaves * 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts * 1 tsp Italian seasoning * 1 lb pasta of choice * ¾ cup heavy cream * Freshly grated Parmesan cheese, to taste * Reserved pasta water, as needed INSTRUCTIONS 1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Add thinly sliced onions to a large baking dish. Drizzle generously with olive oil and season with 1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp salt, ½ tsp pepper, and fresh thyme. Toss everything together. 2. Slice the tops off both heads of garlic, drizzle with olive oil, and nestle them into the onions. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 25 minutes. 3. Meanwhile, season chicken breasts with 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp Italian seasoning, ½ tsp salt, and ½ tsp pepper. 4. Remove the dish from the oven, add the seasoned chicken breasts, cover tightly, and return to the oven for approximately 25 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F. 5. While the chicken cooks, prepare pasta according to package directions. Reserve about 1 cup of pasta water before draining. 6. Remove the chicken from the baking dish and shred. Carefully squeeze the roasted garlic cloves from their skins and mash into the softened onions. 7. Pour in ¾ cup heavy cream and a generous amount of freshly grated Parmesan. Stir until everything is creamy and combined. 8. Add the shredded chicken and cooked pasta. Toss everything together, adding more Parmesan and a splash or two of reserved pasta water as needed. 9. Serve warm with extra Parmesan and enjoy! MY BIG TIP! 🧅 I baked my onions and garlic for just 25 minutes before adding the chicken, and while the finished dish was delicious, they weren't quite as caramelized as I would've liked! If I make this again, I'd give them at least 35–40 minutes in the oven before adding the chicken to develop a deeper flavor. That's what I'd try next time, rather than the 25 minutes I used here! 🤍 #creatorsearchinsights #easydinner #easydinnerideas #pastabake #onepandinner

Trader Joe’s protein pancakes are $3.79 for FOUR… so I made 11 for about $2.43! 👀🥞 And the best part? They have approximately 4.4g of protein per pancake. Made with cottage cheese, oat flour, and a handful of simple ingredients, these are perfect for busy mornings! No gatekeeping here! 🤍 Full recipe below! 🥞 COPYCAT TRADER JOE’S PROTEIN PANCAKES Ingredients: * 1 cup whole-milk cottage cheese * ⅓ cup whole milk * 2 large eggs * ¾ cup oat flour * 2 tbsp brown sugar * 1 tbsp butter, melted * 2 tsp vanilla extract * 1 tsp baking soda * ⅛ tsp sea salt Instructions: 1. Add all ingredients to a blender and blend until completely smooth. 2. Heat a lightly greased nonstick skillet or griddle over medium-low heat. 3. Pour batter onto the skillet, making approximately 3–4-inch pancakes. 4. Cook for about 2–3 minutes, until the edges begin to set and the bottoms are golden brown. 5. Flip carefully and cook for another 1–2 minutes, until golden and cooked through. 6. Repeat with the remaining batter and serve with your favorite toppings! Makes approximately 11 pancakes. 💰 COST + PROTEIN COMPARISON 🥞 Homemade: Approximately $2.43 for 11 pancakes (~22¢ each), with 4.4g protein per pancake. 🥞 Trader Joe’s: $3.79 for 4 pancakes (~95¢ each), with 5g protein per pancake. That's approximately 77% less per pancake! 🙌🏼 Cost and homemade protein estimates will vary depending on ingredient brands and grocery prices. Save this recipe for your next easy, protein-packed breakfast! 🤍 #TraderJoes #ProteinPancakes  #creatorsearchinsights #traderjoesfood  #easymealideas

The Trader Joe’s sheet pan dinner that practically makes itself! 👏🏼🍠 TRADER JOE’S CHICKEN & SWEET POTATO GNOCCHI SHEET PAN Ingredients: * 1–1½ lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs * 1 bag Trader Joe’s pre-cut broccoli florets * 1 bag Trader Joe’s frozen Sweet Potato Gnocchi with Butter & Sage * 2–3 tbsp olive oil, divided For the chicken: * ½ tsp salt * ½ tsp garlic powder * ¼ tsp black pepper * ½ tsp smoked paprika For the broccoli: * ¼ tsp salt * ¼ tsp black pepper * ¼ tsp garlic powder * ¼ tsp dried thyme Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment paper. 2. Drizzle chicken thighs with 1 tbsp olive oil and season both sides with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and smoked paprika. 3. Toss broccoli florets with 1–2 tbsp olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder, and dried thyme. ✨ BROCCOLI TIP: My bag had fairly large broccoli florets, so they roasted perfectly alongside the chicken. If your florets are on the smaller side, wait until the chicken and gnocchi have cooked for about 15 minutes before adding the broccoli to prevent overcooking! 4. Arrange chicken and broccoli on the prepared sheet pan. Add the frozen sweet potato gnocchi, spreading everything into an even layer. 5. Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 175°F internally, the broccoli is roasted and crispy, and the gnocchi is tender. 6. Serve immediately and enjoy! ✨ TIP: Use a large sheet pan and avoid overcrowding so everything roasts instead of steams! Chicken thighs are safe at 165°F, but I love taking mine to 175°F for extra tenderness. LOVE EASY SHEET PAN DINNERS? ❤️ I put together 20 of my favorite sheet pan dinners into one easy guide! That's 4 full weeks of dinners planned for you, with simple ingredients, big flavor, and WAY fewer dishes. Because figuring out what's for dinner every night is exhausting enough. 🙌🏼 Grab my 20 Sheet Pan Dinner Guide through the link in my bio! #TraderJoesRecipes #SheetPanDinner #EasyDinnerIdeas #OnePanMeals  #creatorsearchinsights

#ad SALMON FRIED RICE 🍚🐟Packed with protein, loaded with veggies, and SO easy to throw together! And can we talk about this pan?! I've been loving my @Kaizencookware pan! The cooking surface is made from 100% pure titanium — no nonstick coating, no PFAS, and no PTFE. The trick to cooking with titanium? Properly preheating your pan! Check it out at kaizencookware.com 🤍 ONE-PAN SALMON FRIED RICE Ingredients: * 1 lb skinless salmon fillet * 1–2 tbsp olive oil, for cooking * 1/4 tsp salt * 1/4 tsp black pepper * 1–2 cups broccoli florets, finely chopped * 1/2 cup shredded carrots * 3 green onions, whites and greens separated * 2 large eggs, beaten * 2–2 1/2 cups cooked, cold rice (preferably day-old) * Red pepper flakes, to finish For the sauce: * 4 tbsp soy sauce * 1 tbsp honey * 3 tsp minced garlic * 1 tbsp olive oil Instructions: 1. Preheat your pan: Heat a large skillet over medium heat for 2–3 minutes. Sprinkle a few drops of water onto the surface. If the water forms little beads that dance around the pan, it's ready! Carefully remove any remaining water, then add olive oil. 2. Cook the salmon: Add the whole salmon fillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook for approximately 3 minutes on one side, then flip. Using a spatula, gently break the salmon into bite-sized pieces. 3. Add the veggies: Add the finely chopped broccoli, shredded carrots, and white parts of the green onions. Stir to combine, cover, and cook for approximately 5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the salmon is fully cooked (145°F). 4. Scramble the eggs: Push everything to the sides of the pan, creating a space in the center. Add the beaten eggs and scramble until cooked, then mix everything together. 5. Add the sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, honey, minced garlic, and olive oil. Pour over the salmon and vegetable mixture and stir to combine. 6. Finish with rice: Add the cold, cooked rice and toss everything together. Cook for another 2–3 minutes, until the rice is heated through and evenly coated in sauce. 7. Serve: Finish with red pepper flakes and the green parts of the green onions. Enjoy! #SalmonFriedRice #EasyDinnerIdeas   #creatorsearchinsights #seafoodfriedrice

Replying to @buckweatnoodles The Trader Joe’s dinner that practically makes itself… TERIYAKI edition! 🍚 TRADER JOE’S TERIYAKI CHICKEN & RICE BAKE Part 4 of my Trader Joe’s dinners that practically make themselves! 🤍 Ingredients: * 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs * 1½ cups uncooked jasmine rice * 1 cup Trader Joe’s Soyaki Teriyaki Sauce * 2½ cups chicken broth * ½ red onion, thinly sliced * 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced * Sliced mushrooms * Green beans, trimmed and cut in half (about half a Trader Joe’s bag) * ½ tsp salt * 1 tsp garlic powder * ¼ tsp black pepper * Olive oil, for greasing Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 400°F and lightly grease a 9x13 baking dish with olive oil. 2. Pat chicken thighs dry and season both sides with salt, garlic powder, and black pepper. 3. Add uncooked jasmine rice, Soyaki sauce, chicken broth, red onion, bell pepper, and mushrooms to the prepared baking dish. Stir to combine. 4. Nestle the seasoned chicken thighs into the rice mixture. Cover tightly with aluminum foil and bake for 30–35 minutes. 5. Remove from the oven and give the rice and vegetables a really good stir. Add the halved green beans, cover tightly again, and return to the oven for an additional 15–25 minutes. 6. The chicken should reach at least 175°F, the liquid should be fully absorbed, and the rice should be tender. NOTE: If your rice isn't quite tender, give everything another stir, cover tightly, and bake for an additional 10 minutes. Every oven cooks a little differently! One dish, a handful of Trader Joe’s ingredients, and dinner practically makes itself! 🙌🏼 SAVE this one for your next busy weeknight & FOLLOW for more insanely easy Trader Joe’s dinners! 🤍 #traderjoesr#traderjoesrecipesd#traderjoesdinneri#easydinneridease#onepandinnerrice

Replying to @Katevazz  pesto steak pasta salad recipe — Ingredients (serves 3): 8 oz farfalle pasta  1 large ny strip steak steak seasoning @Kinder's Flavors  1 tbs olive oil @Oliva Dorado  1 tbs butter  fresh rosemary  16 oz cherry tomatoes, halved  12 oz  pre-marinated mozarella balls, halved fresh basil, sliced   1/2 lemon, juiced 1/2 cup pesto 2 cups arugula  salt & pepper to taste  optional: crumbled feta cheese Directions 1. Cook farfalle pasta according to package instructions until al dente. Drain and set aside to cool. 2. Pat steak dry and season generously with steak seasoning. Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear steak for 3–4 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness. Lower heat to medium, add butter, rosemary and baste for 1-2 minutes. Let steak rest for 5–10 minutes before slicing.  3. In a large bowl, combine cooled pasta, halved cherry tomatoes, halved mozzarella balls, sliced fresh basil, and arugula. 4. Add pesto, lemon juice, and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss until everything is evenly coated. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Nyt tarjoan osaamistani myös muille yrityksille ja yrittäjille. ❤️ Olen kasvattanut omia sosiaalisen median kanaviani reilun kahden vuoden ajan ja kerännyt niille yhteensä lähes 50 000 seuraajaa. Pääasialliset kanavani ovat TikTok ja YouTube, mutta minut löytää myös Instagramista käyttäjätunnuksella @sannitoropainen. Matkan varrella olen saanut käytännön kokemusta siitä, millainen sisältö herättää kiinnostusta, saa ihmiset pysähtymään ja parhaimmillaan tavoittaa satojatuhansia katsojia. Olen tehnyt myös kaupallisia yhteistöitä sekä tuottanut sisältöä yritysten sosiaalisen median kanaviin. Minulla on kokemusta yritysten somevideoilla esiintymisestä ja yritysten palveluiden sekä tuotteiden esittelemisestä luontevasti ja kiinnostavasti. Mun vahvuuksia ovat erityisesti: ✨ Lyhytvideot ja Instagram Reels -sisällöt ✨ Tarinallinen kerronta ja käsikirjoittaminen ✨ Huumori ja pilke silmäkulmassa ✨ Arkisten tilanteiden muuttaminen kiinnostavaksi sisällöksi ✨ Ideointi ja luova sisällöntuotanto ✨ Esiintyminen ja luonteva kameran edessä oleminen Tykkään tehdä sisältöä, joka tuntuu aidolta, herättää tunteita ja jää mieleen. Kaiken ei tarvitse olla viimeisen päälle siloteltua tai perinteisen mainosmaista. Joskus juuri ne tavalliset arkiset tilanteet ovat kaikkein kiinnostavinta sisältöä! Mitä voin tehdä yrityksesi somen eteen? Palveluni voidaan räätälöidä juuri yrityksesi tarpeisiin. Voin auttaa esimerkiksi: - Someideoiden ja sisältökonseptien suunnittelussa. - Videoiden ideoinnissa ja käsikirjoittamisessa. - Sisällön kuvaamisessa ja editoinnissa. - Esiintymisessä yrityksen somevideoilla. - Puhelimella otettavien kuvien ja kuvajulkaisujen tuottamisessa. - Julkaisujen suunnittelussa ja julkaisemisessa. - Koko sosiaalisen median sisällöntuotannossa. Voin siis ottaa vastuulleni yksittäisen osa-alueen tai halutessasi hoitaa koko sisällöntuotannon ideasta julkaisuun asti. Millaisella kalustolla työskentelen? Sisällöntuotannossa käytän laadukkaalla kameralla varustettua älypuhelinta, mikrofoneja ja erillistä kuvausvaloa. Videoiden ja kuvien editoinnin teen puhelimella maksullisia editointisovelluksia hyödyntäen. Työskentelyni on ketterää ja erityisesti sosiaalisen median lyhytvideosisältöihin suunniteltua. Miten yhteistyö toimii? Suunnittelemme kokonaisuuden aina yhdessä yrittäjän ja yrityksen kanssa. Sinä tunnet oman yrityksesi ja minä autan tuomaan sen parhaat puolet esiin somessa. Toimin kevytyrittäjänä Y-tunnuksella ja laskutan työni. Yhteistyön laajuus, sisältö ja hinta sovitaan aina tapauskohtaisesti yrityksen tarpeiden mukaan. Asun Riihimäellä, mutta työskentelen mielelläni myös lähialueilla ja sovittaessa myös esim Pääkaupunkiseudulla ja Tampereella. Olisiko sinun yrityksesi somessa tilaa vähän luovemmalle otteelle? Jos kaipaat apua someen, uusia ideoita tai ihan kokonaan somen tekijää, ota rohkeasti yhteyttä! 📩 Yhteydenotot yksityisviestillä tai sähköpostitse: sannitoropainen.media@gmail.com Löydät minut myös somesta: TikTok: @sannitoropainen YouTube: @sannitoropainen Instagram: @sannitoropainen Kaikkea ei tarvitse tehdä itse. 🥤 BATIDO DE FRESAS, BANANA, BLUEBERRIES, MELOCOTÓN Y AVENA 🍓🍌🫐 INGREDIENTES (2 VASOS GRANDES) * 5 fresas medianas * 1 banana * ½ taza de blueberries (arándanos) * 1 melocotón mediano * 1½ tazas de leche regular aproximadamente * ½ taza de leche sabor avena para café (ya endulzada) * 2¼ tazas de avena PREPARACIÓN 1. Lavamos muy bien las fresas y los blueberries. 2. Pelamos la banana y cortamos el melocotón en trozos, retirando el hueso. 3. Colocamos todas las frutas en la licuadora. 4. Agregamos la leche regular y la leche sabor avena para café. 5. Incorporamos la avena. 6. Licuamos muy bien hasta obtener una consistencia cremosa. 7. Servimos en dos vasos grandes y disfrutamos. MI TOQUE ESPECIAL ❤️ La leche sabor avena para café ya tiene su dulcito, así que no necesité agregar azúcar. ¡La combinación de todas las frutas con la avena quedó deliciosa! 💜 purple sweet potato cheesy buns 🍠🧀😋 soft purple buns with a gooey mozzarella, spinach & feta center… and that cheese pull 🤤 only a few ingredients, made in the air fryer would you try this? 👇 recipe (makes 6): dough: 2 medium purple sweet potatoes 1/4 cup milk 1/2 tsp salt 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 cups flour 1 tsp baking powder filling: 1 cup shredded mozzarella 1/3 cup crumbled feta a big handful of spinach, chopped topping: 1 egg yolk + 1 tbsp milk sesame seeds 	1.	bake the sweet potatoes at 400°F for 45–60 min until very soft 	2.	scoop out the flesh and mash with the milk and salt 	3.	mix the flour with the baking powder and add it little by little until the dough is soft and not too sticky 	4.	divide into 6, flatten, add the filling and close into balls 	5.	brush with the yolk + milk and sprinkle with sesame 	6.	air fry at 320°F for 15 min until golden 🥯 send this to someone who needs purple food in their life 💜 save it for later 🤍 #purplesweetpotato #airfryerrecipes #healthyrecipes #easyrecipes #sweetpotatorecipes

Tried a recipe that's almost 300 years old 🎃 A whole chicken baked right inside a pumpkin No pot, no water, and it turns into a real soup What goes inside: a whole chicken cabbage, carrots, onion, mushrooms and a few garlic cloves (any veggies work, celery is great too) fresh rosemary, sage and thyme, bay leaves salt and pepper How I make it: cut off the top of the pumpkin and scoop out the seeds add the veggies, put the chicken on top, then everything else put the lid back on and rub the outside with olive oil bake at 375°F (190°C) for 3 to 4 hours, depending on the size of your pumpkin My tip: the pumpkin holds heat like a thermos, so the inside takes a long time to cook. Always check the chicken with a thermometer, it should reach 165°F (74°C) Once it's done, I shred the meat right into the broth and serve it with the soft pumpkin Save this while it's pumpkin season 👇

High-Protein Berry Buns 🫐🍓 Ingredients for 6 buns: Dough: • 300 g cottage cheese • 90 g flour • 1 egg • 1 egg white • Sweetener to taste • 1/2 tsp baking powder • Pinch of salt Filling: • 100 g Greek yogurt • 1 egg yolk • Vanilla extract • Sweetener, optional • Fresh berries Directions: 1. Mix cottage cheese, egg, egg white, sweetener, salt, and baking powder. 2. Add the flour and mix until a soft dough forms. 3. Divide into 6 pieces, shape into buns, and make a well in the center of each. 4. Mix Greek yogurt, egg yolk, vanilla, and sweetener. 5. Spoon the filling into each bun and top with berries. 6. Bake at 350°F (180°C) for about 20 minutes, until lightly golden.

My Slavic grandma taught me this recipe🥬 And honestly, nothing beats homemade  You’ll need: • 3 kg cabbage (about 2 medium heads) • 150 g carrots • 2 tbsp salt Finely shred the cabbage and grate the carrots. Add the salt and massage everything really well with your hands until the cabbage starts releasing plenty of juice. Pack it tightly into a large 3-liter jar, pressing it down firmly. The cabbage should stay completely covered with its own juice. Leave it at room temperature for 2–3 days. Once or twice a day, pierce the cabbage all the way to the bottom to release the gases. Once it tastes perfectly tangy and fresh, move it to the fridge. A few important tips: • Don’t seal the jar airtight while it’s fermenting. • Keep the cabbage submerged in its juice. • No vinegar needed - this is natural fermentation. • If it tastes too salty, simply add a little more fresh cabbage. Save this recipe and try it at home 🤍
